name: LMOB Benchmark - Local Multi-model Orchestration Benchmark
description: This work presents the LMOB (Local Multi-model Orchestration Benchmark), an experimental study quantifying the trade-off between energy efficiency, latency, and reliability in LLM inference on edge hardware. We compare two inference architecturesfor decomposable tasks: (A) a monolithic 7B-parameter model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) executing the full task, and (B) an orchestrated system composed of a 1.5B router model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) and a 3B specialist model (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct). We executed 50 synthetic system log analysis tasks on an NVIDIA RTX 3060 GPU (12GB VRAM), instrumenting energy via nvidia-smi with trapezoidal integration. Results demonstrate that orchestration reduces energy consumption by 32.7% (276.20 J vs. 410.30 J, 𝑝 < 10−19), but imposes a 31.7% latency penalty (4.800 s vs. 3.644 s, 𝑝 < 10−9) and a 32 percentage point drop in accuracy (Exact Match 68% vs. 100%), due to a phenomenon we term the "Cascading Effect". We project carbon savings of 0.74 grams of CO₂ for the 50-task set, extrapolable to ~5.5 tons/year at data center scale. This work provides the first empirical evidence of an optimization trilemma in local LLM orchestration, offering quantitative parameters for Edge-Cloud system developers (e.g., NVIDIA RTX Spark, Apple Silicon, Windows AI PCs). This work presented the LMOB Benchmark, the first experimental study to quantify the trade-off between energy, latency, and reliability in local orchestration of multiple LLMs on edge hardware.
